MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  AUGUST 19, 2020

CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting of the
City of Rolling Hills Estates at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Stegura, Chan-Southwell, Bacinski,
  Schachter, Uppal, Radocchio

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bain, Larson

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

ALSO PRESENT:  Dan Mabe, AGZA

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, JUNE 3, 2020

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
SCHACTHER to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  JUNE 3, 2020

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CONTINUED DISCUSSION -- CONSIDERATION OF A PROHIBITION OF GASOLINE-
  POWERED LEAF BLOWERS

Planning Manager Naughton stated that at the last EAC meeting, the Committee reviewed the
request to make a recommendation to the City Council to prohibit gas powered leaf blowers. The
Committee directed staff to solicit input from community stakeholders. Staff reported this action
to the City Council at their meeting on June 9, 2020. Staff developed a survey that was sent out
in hopes of reaching a wider audience. At the time of preparing the staff report, there were 40
responses to the survey who were mostly in favor of a more educational approach rather than a
codified prohibition.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is recommending a phased approach, where staff
would first initiate outreach efforts to educate the community about existing rebate and exchange
programs as well as the environmental and public health benefits of using electric powered
equipment; subsequent phases could include more of a compliance approach or an incentive
based approach. Staff would return to the EAC in six months with a progress report where the
Committee could discuss if a different approach should be employed.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided the results of the survey. There were 64 respondents to
the survey with 98% of them being Rolling Hills Estates residents. Ms. Davis stated that the link
was shared with businesses and there has been an effort to schedule calls with businesses in the
commercial district to go over the questions but these attempts to reach businesses have been
unsuccessful

The survey results are as follows:

Q.1.  Which best describes you? 98% residents

 Q.2. Who maintains your lawn/landscape area? Over 50% stated that they utilize a lawn
service; 30% stated that they do some of the work; 15% stated that they care for their own
landscape.

Q.3. Do you own/use any lawn and garden equipment? 48% stated that they own and use
their own equipment; 37% do not own or use lawn and garden equipment; 14% own
equipment, but have not used it.

Q.4. What type of lawn and garden equipment do you or your lawn service use? Leaf blower
90%; lawn mower 73%; lawn edger 67%; brush cutter/hedger 64%; chain saw 42%.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that based on the high use of leaf blowers and lawn mowers
by residents and their lawn service, there is an opportunity to educate on the benefits of using
electric equipment and ensure people are aware of the rebate program.

Q.5. What powers your or your lawn service’s lawn and garden equipment? Gas 53%; Electric
9%; Mix of both 37%.

Q.6. How long do you use these types of equipment in any given use? 54% use their lawn
mower between 11-30 minutes; 45% use their leaf blower between 11-30 minutes.

Q.7. How often do you or your lawn service use this type of equipment? (times per month) 79%
responded 4 times per month; 10% responded 2 times per month; 4% responded 5 or more
times per month.

Q.8. Are you aware of rebate programs available through South Coast Air Quality Management
District (SCAQMD) for the exchange of gas powered equipment for electric powered equipment?
Nearly 90% responded that they were unaware of the program.

Q.9. If you don’t already use electric powered equipment, would you be willing to switch to
electric powered equipment? 60% affirmed that they are willing to switch to electric powered
equipment; 20% indicated that they are not willing to switch.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that some of the comments received were regarding the
feasibility, some commented that they do not believe the batteries last long enough or that their
lawns are too large and electric would not have sufficient power, and some residents don’t think
that their lawn service would be willing to make the switch or that it would be up to their lawn
service. There are opportunities to hold demonstrations of the various electric equipment options.

Q.10. To consider transitioning from gasoline to powered lawn equipment to electric, the City
should (Select any you agree with). 62% selected educate residents; 29% selected gasoline
equipment should not be prohibited; 25% selected prohibit only gasoline leaf blowers; 11%
prohibit all gasoline equipment.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that this also shows that it is a matter getting information out
to the community to help them make an educated decision. The survey was sent via social media,
HOA’s, directly to business license contractors.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI expressed his concern with the survey only capturing 1% of
the city’s population. CHAIR SCHMITZ agreed.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that neighboring cities have prohibited gas powered
equipment and are enforcing this. As lawn care businesses become aware of this, it may help the
city educate these businesses and make the transition to electric equipment easier.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI asked how the education approach would be different, as far
as response, to the survey. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the survey response was
limited to a short timeframe, as opposed to education which would be a six-month window. Also,
with more time, there is more opportunity to find ways to make the information accessible to the
public.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that because it is a small sample size, the education
would be preferable. If the rebate program is part of the education being provided, then that may
get more attention.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA inquired if it is possible to require that they have a city
business license prior to applying for the rebate. Planning Manager Naughton stated that since
the rebate program is directly through the SCAQMD, the City does not have approval authority.
Assistant City Manager Davis added that this is possible if the City has their own rebate program.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, AUGUST 19, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO agreed and stated that educating people first will give
opportunity for people to buy in to the idea as opposed to prohibiting, where people may feel like
they were not given an opportunity to provide input.

A brief discussion ensued.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
RADOCCHIO to,

  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL THE EDUCATIONAL APPROACH TO
  ELECTRIC POWERED EQUIPMENT AND REPORT BACK TO THE COMMITTEE IN SIX
  MONTHS.

AYES:  Schmitz, Radocchio, Chan-Southwell, Stegura, Bacinski, Schachter, Uppal
NOES:
ABSENT:  Bain, Larson
ABSTAIN:

B.  AGZA GREEN ZONE CERTIFICATION

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief introduced Dan Mabe, AGZA and provided a brief
overview on the AGZA Green Zone Certification program. The program is funded by the South
Coast Air Quality Management Distrcit (SCAQMD). AGZA is a leader in zero emissions
sustainable grounds maintenance strategies. Ernie Howlett Park could be a green zone site and
would provide the city to lead by example and begin transitioning city-owned equipment to electric.
In addition, provide opportunities for contractors to see the city’s site as a demonstration site. Staff
has the idea to begin small within the city and then possibly have the other cities on the peninsula
become green zone certified.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that the recommendation would be to begin with Ernie
Howlett Park as the green zone site, there would be an audit and report on health and
environmental impacts, a recommendation on the type of electric equipment that the city could
transition to, and education and demonstration opportunities.

Dan Mabe, Founder and President, AGZA, provided a presentation on the program. The first part
of the program includes the AGZA Green Zone Certification Program, which includes, a gas
inventory is taken of the property and an impact report is provided. The AGZA Service
Professional Certification has to do with transitioning crews including training and certification.
The AGZA Initiatives includes assistance with exchange programs.

Mr. Mabe stated that the impact reports are recognized by the California Air Resources Board
and the EPA has acknowledged some of their reports. A cost of operation comparison was
provided for gas and electric equipment.

Mr. Mabe stated that AGZA is monetized by the SCAQMD. AGZA is available to coordinate and
conduct workshops. In addition, if the city would desire, an AGZA certified green zone could be
established.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO inquired on the smaller types of lawn mowers. Mr. Mabe
stated that the life cycle cost savings percentage would be similar to the larger equipment.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO inquired on the power of the electric leaf blowers as
opposed to the gas leaf blowers. Mr. Mabe stated that the electric leaf blowers fall short of the
gas leaf blowers. However, the electric leaf blowers are able to handle most workloads.

COMMITTEE BACINSKI asked about the how AGZA is funded. Mr. Mabe stated that they are
monetized by air districts, non-profits, and municipalities.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Mr. Mabe stated that their
contract with SCAQMD is approximately as $70K per year.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL asked if there is a limit on how many rebates a business can
receive. Mr. Mabe stated that he does not believe there is a limit if the applicant meets all the
requirements.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL asked if there is an electric equipment rebate. Mr.
Mabe stated that the rebate program is gas to electric and stated that this is how his company

 assists with exchange programs in order to understand workload performance verification before
purchasing/exchanging equipment.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA inquired about the certification process, which includes
advising on charging and storage facilities and asked if the city would be responsible for
constructing these. Mr. Mabe stated that the charging and storage facilities are not included and
the City may need to modify the charging infrastructure. AGZA will provide guidance and
recommendations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked about the benefit of having the AGZA certification. Mr.
Mabe stated that it provides a way to verify and quantify and measure environmental impact
improvements and can lead to grants. Mr. Mabe stated that the certification has been recognized
by members of congress and senators. There are also local politicians and SCAQMD board
members who are in favor of this certification since it acts as a mechanism for verified
implementation.

Planning Manager Naughton added that the Sustainability Element is being started as well as the
Climate Adaptation Plan and having a program like the Green Certification Zone could help with
goals of the Sustainability Element.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO to,

  RECOMMEND THE AGZA GREEN CERTIFICATION PROGRAM TO THE CITY
  COUNCIL TO PARTICIPATE USING ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AS ITS FIRST GREEN
  ZONE SITE.

AYES:  Schmitz, Radocchio, Chan-Southwell, Stegura, Schachter, Uppal
NOES:  Bacinski
ABSENT:  Bain, Larson
ABSTAIN:

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that this presentation will go before the City Council on September 8,
2020.
